title: Application Has Crashed
shortDescription: Common PS4 crash error returning user to home.
fullDescription: CE-34878-0 is the most common PS4 error, indicating a game has crashed. Causes range from outdated firmware to a failing hard drive.

fixSteps.title: Update game
fixSteps.instruction: Highlight game, Options > Check for Update.

fixSteps.title: Replace HDD with SSD
fixSteps.instruction: Swap 2.5 inch drive; reinstall system software.

title: Cannot Start Application Hard Drive
shortDescription: PS4 cannot read from internal hard drive.
fullDescription: CE-30005-8 is a hard drive read error. Usually means HDD is failing.

fixSteps.title: Reseat drive
fixSteps.instruction: Remove HDD bay, reseat HDD into SATA connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace HDD
fixSteps.instruction: Install new SSD or HDD, reinstall system software.

faq.a: Only if PS Plus cloud backup or USB backup before swap.

title: System Update File Not Found
shortDescription: Update via USB cannot find file.
fullDescription: SU-41350-3 occurs when the USB folder structure is incorrect. The file must be at PS4/UPDATE/PS4UPDATE.PUP.
symptoms: USB update fails to detect file

fixSteps.title: Correct path
fixSteps.instruction: Create PS4/UPDATE folder, place PS4UPDATE.PUP inside.

faq.a: Some PS4s reject exFAT for system update; FAT32 safest.

title: PSN Server Communication Failed
fullDescription: NP-34957-8 indicates PSN connection failure. Could be PSN outage, NAT, or DNS.

faq.a: Sometimes if ISP blocks PSN ports.

title: Account Banned From PSN
fullDescription: WS-37397-9 indicates a console-level ban. Usually caused by chargebacks, modding, or piracy.
symptoms: No account can sign in on this console

fixSteps.title: Contact Sony support
fixSteps.instruction: Call PlayStation support to inquire about the ban.

title: Blue Light of Death (BLOD)
shortDescription: PS4 power LED pulses blue and no display.
fullDescription: BLOD is a hardware handshake failure between PS4 and display. Often caused by HDMI cable, sleep-mode bug, or APU solder issues.

fixSteps.title: Test HDMI cable and TV port

title: PS4 Continually Beeps and Ejects Disc
shortDescription: Console beeps and ejects on its own.
fullDescription: Phantom eject is caused by a sticky touch-sensor or warped chassis pressing the eject button. Solution: remove screw under sticker on bottom.

fixSteps.title: Remove screw under warranty sticker
fixSteps.instruction: Tilt console; remove screw at bottom under sticker. Voids warranty.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If still occurs, replace eject sensor board.

title: Cannot Find Update File on USB
fullDescription: Similar to SU-41350-3, but during reinstall. Verify FAT32 USB and proper path.

fixSteps.title: Use PS4UPDATE.PUP reinstall version
fixSteps.instruction: Download PS4 reinstall (full) PUP, not update PUP.

faq.a: Update PUP for online updates; reinstall PUP for full reflash.

title: Error Has Occurred in System Software
fullDescription: Generic system error often resolved by restarting and updating system software.

faq.a: Some users report after unsupported USB drive.

title: PS4 Pro Sounds Like a Jet
fullDescription: Loud fan often means dust buildup, thermal paste degradation, or dying liquid metal on Pro.

fixSteps.title: Compressed air
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out vents and fan from outside.

fixSteps.title: Disassemble and clean fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove top, clean fan blades and heatsink.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermal paste
fixSteps.instruction: Apply quality thermal paste to APU.

faq.a: PS4 Pro APU does not use liquid metal; PS5 does.
